items.title: Closed runtime evidence envelope
items.statement: A valid instance is a JSON object with no undeclared top-level properties. It must carry the twelve named required fields; schema_id and artifact_type are fixed constants; identifiers are nonempty where constrained; routing_refs must contain at least one nonempty string; and type_payload must be an object with at least one property.

items.title: Operational fields have presence but no domain semantics
items.statement: created_at_utc, projection_freshness, projection_health, retention_class, and source_surface are only strings; the contract does not constrain timestamp syntax, freshness or health vocabularies, retention values, or cross-field consistency.
items.impact: Different producers can emit schema-valid but mutually incompatible operational metadata, preventing deterministic retention, health, and freshness decisions.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent timestamp parsing, enumerations, and consistency rules or accept arbitrary nonempty values for the required fields.

items.title: Trust, ownership, consumer, and privacy semantics are absent
items.statement: producer_ref and actor_ref are optional opaque strings, no owner or consumer is required, and the schema defines no authorization, confidentiality, integrity, provenance-validation, or redaction rules for references or payload content.
items.impact: Schema validity cannot establish who may produce or consume evidence, who owns it, whether references are authentic, or whether payload data is safe to retain and expose.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose trust boundaries, identity resolution, access controls, ownership, consumer routing, and privacy treatment outside this contract.

items.title: Lifecycle, propagation, recovery, migration, and bounds are unspecified
items.statement: The schema fixes a v1 identity and validates routing_refs and an open type_payload shape, but it supplies no artifact state machine, failure or recovery model, reference-resolution or propagation guarantees, version migration rules, payload subtype discrimination, or collection and payload size limits.
items.impact: Implementations can disagree on lifecycle transitions, retry or repair behavior, routing integrity, payload interpretation, version evolution, and safe resource limits while remaining schema-valid.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent lifecycle, propagation, recovery, subtype dispatch, migration, and resource-bound behavior.

dimension_assessments.summary: The line defines exact JSON validation behavior for the top-level evidence envelope.
The envelope can carry evidence identity, project/run/attempt binding, routing references, operational labels, and a type-specific payload.
The schema precisely defines the accepted JSON instance shape and validation outcome boundary.
Required fields, constants, closed top-level properties, routing minimums, and payload minimums are explicit.
No evidence lifecycle states or transitions are defined.
Opaque optional actor and producer references do not define authority or authorization.
No required owner or ownership-transfer semantics exist.
No consumer identity, entitlement, or consumption contract is specified.
This line is a runtime data-envelope schema and specifies no user-visible GUI presentation.
No invalid-reference, routing, payload, retry, repair, or recovery behavior is defined beyond schema rejection.
The schema has no access-control, integrity, confidentiality, sensitivity, or redaction semantics.
Routing and receipt references are structurally present but their resolution and propagation guarantees are unspecified.
Freshness, health, retention, timestamp, and source-surface values lack operational domains and cross-field rules.
Reference arrays and type_payload have no maximum sizes or complexity bounds.
A v1 identity is fixed, but compatibility negotiation and migration behavior are absent.
Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema validation is a deterministic structural acceptance oracle for this envelope.
Builders retain consequential discretion over operational vocabularies, authority, ownership, security, lifecycle, routing, migration, subtype dispatch, and bounds.
Multiple schema-valid implementations can assign incompatible semantics to opaque strings, references, operational fields, and payload content.
